title: Why McLaren went the opposite way to Mercedes' front wing
excerpt:
Just underscoring the idea that what works for one car won’t necessarily be good for another, McLaren have made precisely the opposite change in their front wing philosophy to that recently made by Mercedes.

The new McLaren wing in Sao Paulo is joined to the nose via the middle of the three elements rather than the bottom element used previously. Mercedes made the opposite change at the recent US Grand Prix.

title: Alonso credits ‘phenomenal’ car after strong drive in Brazil
excerpt:
After a difficult time of it in Mexico City, Aston Martin bounced back strongly in Brazil as Fernando Alonso finished 12th at Interlagos, just missing out on a rare chance to score points.

The Spaniard showed all his experience in the wet on Saturday to qualify inside the top 10 for the first time all season, and managed to remain up the order in the first stint of the race in what he called a “phenomenal” car.

Even after he started to drop backwards, Alonso was able to fight with the cars around him, which included some of the more typical front runners – the Aston Martin man overtaking Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari on merit at one point.

While his drive did not yield any points, it still left Alonso in a buoyant mood post-race.

“I think it was the best race for the car feeling today," he said. "The car was phenomenal in the corners and we were battling with the Ferraris at one point.

“Even the last five laps on the inters, we were in the mix with the two Mercedes, one lap down, but with the Mercedes. Taking into account how much we lose on the straights, that means probably today we could have been maybe one second faster than them per lap. As I said the car was phenomenal.”

While Alonso’s ‘one second faster’ comment seemed tongue in cheek, what was clear was how much quicker the AMR26 was in Brazil than it has been for much of the season.

His drive was also a good response to Mexico City, where the team had to retire both cars early on with power unit problems, and Alonso’s Sao Paulo performance saw him beat both Alpines, both Williams cars and the two Haas drivers to the flag on merit.

5 Winners and 5 Losers from Sao Paulo

Lance Stroll, however, did not make the end of the race – retiring again with an ERS issue for his eighth DNF in the last 10 Grands Prix.

But Chief Trackside Officer Mike Krack was upbeat in the wake of the race, choosing to look at the weekend as a whole.

“Mixed fortunes for us today," he explained. "A strong drive from Fernando to finish P12 and Lance unfortunately retiring with a battery issue.

"Overall we must be satisfied with the outcome of the weekend as we were ahead of competitors with faster cars in Qualifying and race.”

“We always look forward to racing here in Sao Paulo – an iconic track with a passionate crowd - so it was great to deliver a strong performance in front of the Brazilian fans.”

Aston Martin remain 10th in the standings, five points adrift of Williams.

Alonso last scored in Malaysia, but Aston Martin are seemingly heading in the right direction on pace, even if reliablity remains an Achilles' heel.

title: P10 in Sao Paulo GP 'the maximum possible' – Hulkenberg
excerpt:
Nico Hulkenberg believes that P10 and the final point on offer was "the maximum possible" in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, the Audi driver having recovered from a 10-second penalty.

Hulkenberg lined up fourth on the grid for last Sunday's 71-lap race in Brazil, the German having starred in a wet Qualifying session and promoted two spots by grid penalties for George Russell and Charles Leclerc.

The Audi racer eventually slipped down the order in the Grand Prix as wet conditions at the start soon dried, and found himself battling Franco Colapinto's Alpine on fringes of the points.

Hulkenberg moved ahead at Turn 1 but only after cutting the track, meaning he received a 10-second penalty, which the German served at a late pit stop as drivers pitted for intermediate tyres amid another rain shower.

Having dropped to P11, Hulkenberg charged after Arvid Lindblad before passing the Racing Bulls driver seven laps from the end.

"It was a good move [on Lindblad], set him up a little bit on the entry for the exit with an undercut. It felt nice, felt good, especially after the penalty, obviously to fight back for that position," said Hulkenberg.

"I think that was the maximum possible really today. We didn't have that much pace to offer on the slick or the intermediates, so we'll have to take that and review."

The result was only Hulkenberg's fifth time in the points during a Grand Prix this season, with Audi reducing the gap to Haas for P7 in the teams' standings down to just three points.

Team mate Gabriel Bortoleto finished P16, the Brazilian home hero having crashed out early in Qualifying, which ultimately left him P19 on the grid.

"When I was able to be in free air and put some pace out there [it] was very positive," he said.

"But obviously it's a consequence of yesterday, starting from the back you need to overtake people. Was not easy to overtake because obviously we are limited by the power that we have when it's raining, so we're limited to 250Kw.

"Difficult to get some top speed difference on the straight and I got a bit stuck behind other cars, and when I managed to get free air the pace was very positive and also in the wet at the end, when we put on the inter was very good.

"It's a shame, I think home race was not how I expected. The love from the fans was there and I really appreciate it, so we go to the next one."

title: The best images from Mercedes' title celebrations
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli might have sealed the drivers' title in Mexico City, but it took one race longer for Mercedes to claim their ninth Constructors' Championship title.

The Silver Arrows won the teams' title in Sao Paulo, courtesy of George Russell's fourth-place finish, with Antonelli in fifth. That was more than enough to beat Ferrari, who had both cars down the order.

As such, Mercedes took their first constructors' title since 2021, and the celebrations at track were special. After seeing Red Bull win in 2022 and 2023, and then McLaren take back-to-back titles, Mercedes were clearly very, very happy to be back at the pinacle of the sport.

title: Rivals congratulate Mercedes on Constructors' Championship
excerpt:
Mercedes' wait for another Constructors' Championship ended last weekend, as the German manufacturer achieved the feat at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

The Silver Arrows only needed to outscore main rivals Ferrari by a handful of points in Brazil, with P4 for George Russell and P5 for new World Champion Kimi Antonelli proving more than enough.

The title is Mercedes' first as a team since 2021, while the success in 2026 brings their total count up to nine constructors' titles, joint with Williams and third behind only Ferrari (16) and McLaren (10).

"I'm so proud for the organisation," said Team Principal Toto Wolff after the race in Brazil.

"We've taken a few years to be back on the top spot. Not many teams have been able to come back from such a situation.

"And it just shows that, you know, the great work, the great people that we have in our organisation. And it's fantastic to be among them."

Mercedes' success came under the new-for-2026 regulations, which included drastic overhauls to both the aerodynamics and power units of the cars.

Mercedes' Trackside Engineering Director Andrew Shovlin admitted that "we've never put so much effort into a new set of regulations" before.

He said: "We had periods where it looked like we were going to get there [win another title], and then you weren't, and you have all these setbacks. When you've finally done it again, it's just immensely satisfying.

"And, you know, no one gave up. They just kept pushing, kept working hard. There was obviously a big rule change this year. We've never put so much effort into a new set of regulations."

Rivals up and down the grid offered their congratulations to the new World Champions, including McLaren, the Woking-based outfit having lost their crown from last season.

All the key moments from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix

McLaren CEO Zak Brown posted on X: "Congratulations to Mercedes and HPP on securing the Constructors’ Championship title after an impressive season. Looking forward to fighting you for it again next year."

Team Principal Andrea Stella added during a post-race media session: "[I want to] congratulate Mercedes on winning the Constructors’ Championship. Formula 1 is operating, like I've been saying for some time, at very, very high level, very high standards.

"So to be able to win in this kind of competitive context is a reflection of great work that must have happened at Mercedes, so they deserve to be certainly acknowledged."

Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton, who won six of his seven drivers' titles with Mercedes and was at the team as it won eight consecutive teams' titles, posted on Instagram: "Congratulations guys, am so happy for you all. So well deserved."

Red Bull Team Principal Laurent Mekies added in his post-race media session: "I think they have done an outstanding job. We all recall how dominant they were at the start of the season.

"And of course, we knew they had switched earlier than most [last year to focus on 2026], but it's something to switch earlier than most, something else to convert it into lap time, and that's what they have done.

"And you know they started the season with more than a second advantage on us, so they have obviously done a very good job, so well done to them."

Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali also gave his congratulations to the latest winners in the championship.

“My huge congratulations to everyone at the Mercedes Formula 1 Team on becoming 2026 Constructors’ World Champions. Reaching the summit of Formula 1 is never the achievement of one person alone," he said.

"It is the result of extraordinary talent, relentless determination and the shared belief of hundreds of people, at the circuit and back at the factory, all united by the same ambition. Every single member of this team should feel incredibly proud of what they have achieved.

"This is also a moment that will have a special place in the history of our sport. With his ninth Constructors’ title, my friend Toto Wolff draws level with the great Sir Frank Williams, one of Formula 1’s true legends. To stand alongside Frank in the record books is an extraordinary achievement and a powerful testament to Toto’s leadership, vision and relentless pursuit of excellence over so many years.

"To win the Constructors’ Championship in the same season that Kimi Antonelli became the youngest ever Drivers’ World Champion makes 2026 truly unforgettable for Mercedes and for Formula 1. This is what our sport is all about: dreaming big, pushing beyond the limits, and proving what is possible when great people come together with one shared purpose.

"Mercedes have returned to the very top, and in doing so have written another remarkable chapter in the history of Formula 1.”

title: How Verstappen outperformed Red Bull’s simulations in Brazil
excerpt:
The Sao Paulo Grand Prix was a superb race for Red Bull Racing as Max Verstappen put in an extraordinary charge from 21st on the grid to second, and Isack Hadjar backed him up with a solid third place.

What made Verstappen’s progress through the field so impressive was that the man himself had cautioned that with the 2026 cars, passing would not be as easy as he had previously demonstrated at Interlagos.

And yet he somehow found the performance that he needed, even if at times he made it clear that he wasn’t happy with the balance of the RB22.

Team Principal Laurent Mekies confirmed that the Dutchman had outperformed Red Bull’s pre-race expectations.

“As always, I think no sim in the world would predict that you go from P21 to P2, or that you get 14 places in five laps,” he said. “There is no sim being able to do that. So he's beating the sim on a regular basis!”

The obvious disappointment was that Verstappen had to start from the back of the grid, something that was not anticipated going into the weekend.

“Of course it's frustrating, because the pace seemed good on Friday and also on Saturday morning, and in some respects in Q1 when we let him qualify,” said Mekies.

“But it's part of the game. It's easy to forget, it's the first year with the power unit, and the guys have been doing an extraordinary job. And we take the first penalty with Max this weekend, and that's what it is. It was not planned. We had a small issue on Friday that forced us to do so.”

Intriguingly Mekies conceded that it was not a given that Verstappen could have beaten winner Lando Norris, even if he’d started at the sharp end.

“Well done to Lando and to McLaren,” said the Frenchman. “I think they were generally a bit faster than us in the race. I also think that even if you start P2, say, I think on pace Lando was anyway a bit a bit faster than us.

“So of course it's a different story if you start P2, because you have all the first opening laps risk taking, on which Max is unbelievable. But I think they were a bit faster than us.”

Mekies couldn’t say definitively why that was: “Is it degradation? Is it pure pace? Obviously, they brought another fair bit of upgrade this weekend again. Or is it something else?

“Because you may have heard Max being fairly vocal with the car balance once we had switched to dry tyres, and from that point onward, he has been very, very unhappy with car balance, including when we came back to the inters at the very end.

“So we need to analyse what happened there, how much of that is time loss, and whether or not that would have been enough to fight with McLaren.”

On his charge through the field, Verstappen was helped by Hadjar letting him through. Mekies admits that there was an option to swap the places back later on, but it didn’t happen.

Verstappen reflects on 'challenging' P21 to podium charge

“I think we would have done it if the cars had stayed close together,” he noted. “We would have done it, because Isack had a very strong pace and he stayed with Max, as you have seen after the swap.

“But then, as the race panned out and the rain came again, the cars were very, very distant, and it would not have made sense. Plus, increased rain intensity at the end, it would not have made any sense. But I have to say, Max and Isack worked very, very strongly together to give us that result.”

Hadjar may have been disappointed not to have been able to finish ahead of his team mate, but nevertheless Interlagos was another strong performance, making good progress after struggling to find the right setup earlier in the weekend.

“I think ultimately, if you ask me right now, I think it's the best race he has done with us in terms of pure pace, and that's what we look at,” said Mekies. “Pure pace on the dries, on the inters, super difficult conditions, in how clever he has been racing. He has done a lot of very strong racing this year, but I think he has raised the bar another time.

“So that's what we want to keep seeing. That's what we said we were most impressed by when we took the decisions to confirm him for '27, the way he keeps raising the bar, and we were simply hoping to provide him with the environment for him to keep doing that. I think he has done that today in terms of the race, and in the context where he has been building through the weekend.”

A win for McLaren coming just a week after an event that saw Ferrari on pole and in contention for victory was another sign of just how competitive F1 currently is at the front of the grid, with the top four teams evenly matched.

“The convergence is probably happening earlier than what we all thought,” said Mekies. “I'm guessing somehow it's perhaps an indication of fairly restrictive regulations. That being said, you see cars with visibly different concepts, and you see four top teams fighting, which is probably a great point to be for the sport.

“So, let's see how it will pan out in the second year. But it's fair to say that having to be already in the second part of '26 in the situation where you turn up at the race weekend, and you don't know which one of the four top teams is going to win the race, I think it's great for the sport.

“And yes, we get now top five in Qualifying separated by two-tenths, and it's a strong combination of development race and absolute perfect execution if you want to win on Sunday.”

title: Stella reveals how McLaren triumphed at Interlagos
excerpt:
The Sao Paulo Grand Prix was a race of tyres and the challenge getting them into the right window, whether they be the intermediates used at the start and finish, or the soft slicks deployed in the middle part of the race.

Lando Norris and McLaren did a better job than anyone else across a very difficult afternoon of changing conditions, and they reaped the reward with a superb victory.

Team Principal Andrea Stella conceded that the cooler conditions in Interlagos on Sunday tipped the balance in favour of the MCL40.

"My explanation of our performance in dry today is associated with the track and ambient temperature,” said the Italian post-race.

“The conditions were very cold, much colder than we had in practice. In practice, I think we saw that we were still tending to overheat the tyres. Today, somehow the conditions came our way, and we could keep the tyre temperature under control. I think that's the main reason.

“We know that we have some work to do in terms of getting more consistent in long runs in hot conditions, and I think we were in a way helped.

“You could see also this well, especially with Lando, when the track was getting greasy before switching onto intermediate tyres. Lando was just able to keep the lap times much better than anybody else, and I think our car is good from this point of view."

It wasn’t entirely straightforward, however. Stella noted that some cars were more competitive at various stages of the afternoon.

“I think what we have seen is that cars exhibited different features,” he said. “Like at the start of the race, you needed to be good at bringing the tyres into temperature.

“In the laps to the grid, nobody could actually generate any temperature. So definitely, in the early laps, there was a premium to the cars, or the drivers, that were able to generate tyre temperature.

“Obviously Max [Verstappen], likewise Lewis [Hamilton], I think they have shown their talent not only from a tyre switching on point of view, but also in the first lap. I watched some images; they were just incredible how easily they gained positions.

“But going back to the evolution of the race, I think something we have seen [Saturday], even in Qualifying, we seemed to be good when there was a lot of water, and then we kind of lost it a little bit in Q2 when there was less water.

“Likewise today, it was difficult to see a car that was good in all conditions. We struggled a bit more with Lando at the start, and then somehow we managed to keep good grip in the intermediate tyres, and also on the soft tyres.

“I think in the final part of the stint on the soft tyres, Lando was very fast, and probably there he is the one that had done the best job. Because if you look at [Kimi] Antonelli as well, he was good at the final part of the stint on soft, and he struggled at the start, and he lost position.

“So, it was technically a very interesting race, because really everyone had to deal at some stage with the tyres being either too cold or getting too hot, but without a clear pattern. All teams will have some data to look into, and understand.”

One of the intriguing aspects of the race came in the slick tyre stint, as drivers discussed the possibility of running to the end on their original set, with Norris and McLaren among those to have such a conversation.

However as those who changed to fresh rubber showed good pace, rivals were obliged to follow suit.

“Antonelli decided to go for another stop, and this made our life a little easier from this point of view,” said Stella. “I don't think at any stage we thought that we could have gone all the way to the end.

“Russell, I think, is the only one that took advantage for staying on the same set and going on to intermediate tyres. This was a consideration, but we were unsure as to how the rain would have actually manifested itself. So we decided with both drivers to go for the more rational approach, which was just go on another set.”

Norris delighted to 'give back' to McLaren in Sao Paulo win

It wasn’t all about tyres, however, and Stella paid tribute to Norris, who has a great feel for low grip conditions.

“You're never going to have a really perfect car, you're never going to have the perfect conditions,” said Stella. “So adaptability is actually probably the most important feature that you may want to possess as a driver.

"I think that should be definitely acknowledged and recognised for Lando, when there's a need to understand what's best, how to operate, he is definitely a master.

“Hopefully we don't need to rely on these qualities though, we just want to make sure that we can offer Lando and Oscar [Piastri] a competitive car such that they can just drive a little bit more easily, because still our car remains pretty difficult.”

Norris won twice in the summer at the Hungaroring and Zandvoort, and he looked set to triumph in Madrid before getting caught out by the Virtual Safety Car. Since then, McLaren have been outperformed by their rivals, and thus a victory late in the season was most welcome.

It bodes well for the Interlagos upgrade package, the first part of a step towards the 2027 car that the team has fast tracked for this season.

“As for the McLaren trajectory, after the upgrades in Hungary, it was encouraging that we were in position to win,” said Stella. “We should have won Madrid, really. But after that, other people took upgrades, and we lost this position. I think we also paid the price on not having had great Qualifying sessions.

“It would have been interesting to see Lando starting from the front in races like Austin or Mexico. I think it would have been definitely a fight for podium, but it's thanks to these upgrades that we are now in condition to fight for the victory, combined with the conditions surely.”

There’s more to come for the next race: “And these upgrades, first of all, they will be complemented by some more parts that come in Vegas, and they form the foundation for what will be next year's car.

“So it's encouraging for the trajectory of McLaren that we seem to be able to transform our development into performance on track, and it's also important for McLaren that we had solid pit stops because we don't come from a period of consistent pit stops, and also execution in these mixed conditions.

“Because we have had some disappointing races, like in Canada, where we were starting with the intermediate tyres, and the double extra formation lap was unlucky, honestly.

"So it's good that we were able to master these conditions at the pit wall as well. And I'm very proud to have seen the team operate at this very high level.”

title: Piastri and management team mutually terminate agreement
excerpt:
McLaren driver Oscar Piastri has split from his management team, led by nine-time Grand Prix winner Mark Webber and his partner Ann Webber.

A joint statement on the Monday after the Sao Paulo Grand Prix said the two sides had "mutually agreed to terminate their management agreement".

Nine-time winner Piastri, who is competing in his fourth season in F1, said: "I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years.

"Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward."

Former Red Bull, Williams and Jaguar driver Mark Webber added: "We are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of Oscar's career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early on.

"Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close.

"This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure, and for us to embark on our new ventures. We wish Oscar all the very best for a long and successful career."

Norris wins Sao Paulo GP thriller as Mercedes claim title

The Webbers started working with Piastri in 2019, when the Australian won his first single-seater championship with victory in the Formula Renault Eurocup as well as securing a spot on the Renault F1 Team's junior programme.

The 25-year-old went on to win the FIA Formula 3 Championship title the next season and followed that up with a title win in the FIA Formula 2 Championship in 2021.

Renault's rebranded Alpine team squandered the chance to promote Piastri from reserve to a full-time race seat, leaving the door open for the Australian to find a seat elsewhere.

Mark Webber opened talks with McLaren and secured a deal for Piastri to make his F1 debut with the British team in 2023 as a replacement for fellow Australian Daniel Ricciardo.

It proved a decisive move for the Australian's career. Piastri took two podiums in his rookie season and secured his first Grand Prix win the following year in Hungary.

Piastri then launched an impressive title charge in a third campaign with McLaren in 2025 before ultimately losing out to team mate Lando Norris.

The Webbers took a step back from a front-line role with Piastri this year and went from having a regular presence at track to only making fleeting appearances.

Piastri's former race engineer at Prema, Pedro Matos, and his mental coach, Emma Murray, have since taken on a greater role at track as part of the Australian's close team.

And as per the statement on Monday, Piastri – who currently sits seventh in the Drivers' Championship – will operate under a new management structure going forward.

title: FIA reaffirms commitment to ending F1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi
excerpt:
The FIA and its President, Mohammed Ben Sulayem, have reiterated their stance that the F1 season will end as planned in the Middle East.

The campaign-concluding triple header is scheduled to see the paddock head from Las Vegas to Qatar and finally to Abu Dhabi.

However, the instability in the Middle East after the start of the United States-Iran war in March has caused considerable uncertainty across the year.

Whilst it has become clearer in recent weeks that Formula 1 can — and most likely will — finish the calendar as designed, there are contingency plans in place.

Imola is on standby to hold a one-off round in place of the finale in early December if F1 does not deem it ultimately safe to visit Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

MotoGP held a round in the former nation last weekend, which should provide further reassurance that the final two F1 weekends can go ahead.

Although the region remains volatile, there has not been a recent escalation in hostilities between the United States and Iran, which led to strikes across the Gulf earlier in 2026.

That not only affected travel to the season-opening Australian Grand Prix, but also saw the rescheduling and relocating of the Bahrain Grand Prix to Malaysia in October and the outright cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix.

But as F1 prepares to head back to the Middle East for the first time since pre-season testing, the FIA has reaffirmed the decision with a statement of support.

"The countdown is on for Qatar and Abu Dhabi," Ben Sulayem wrote on a social media post. "We are fully focused on delivering two exceptional grand prix weekends.

"We are working closely with our partners to ensure everything is in place for our drivers, teams and fans.

"We look forward to welcoming everyone for two thrilling weekends of racing and an unforgettable finish to the Formula 1 season."

title: Red Bull retain shock status as FIA make key 2027 F1 announcement
excerpt:
Red Bull-Ford will enter the 2027 Formula 1 season without additional power unit development allowances after the FIA confirmed that its latest ADUO assessment has resulted in no further upgrades being granted.

The decision leaves Red Bull, which was surprisingly identified as the benchmark for internal combustion engine (ICE) performance earlier this year, without the additional homologation opportunities awarded to rival manufacturers.

The FIA has completed its third Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) review of 2026, covering races 12 to 18, with the findings communicated to all five power unit manufacturers.

Although the governing body confirmed that the performance gaps between the manufacturers had changed, no additional homologations were awarded.

It marks the second consecutive review without any further upgrades being granted, leaving the existing allocations unchanged heading into 2027.

Red Bull-Ford's position as the benchmark came as a shock earlier in the campaign, particularly given Mercedes' dominance under the new regulations and Red Bull's status as a first-year engine manufacturer.

However, the FIA's assessment measures ICE performance rather than the complete hybrid power unit, with Red Bull emerging as the benchmark in the opening assessments.

[Article continues below]

How does ADUO work?

Introduced for 2026, ADUO allows manufacturers whose internal combustion engines fall at least two per cent below the leading ICE to undertake additional development.

Manufacturers between two and four per cent behind qualify for one additional homologation in the current season and another the following year, alongside an increased cost cap and dynamometer testing allowances.

Those at least four per cent behind qualify for two additional homologations in each season.

Following the first review, which concluded after the Canadian Grand Prix, Mercedes was placed in the two-to-four per cent category, earning one additional upgrade for 2026 and another for 2027.

Audi, Ferrari and Honda were all more than four per cent behind, qualifying for two additional homologations in each season.

Red Bull received no additional allowances, while the second review, completed after the Hungarian Grand Prix, also produced no further allocations.

The latest findings therefore leave those original allowances intact for 2027, with Red Bull still without any extra development opportunities under ADUO.

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis defended the assessment process, saying the governing body was confident in its conclusions.

He also acknowledged that discussions were ongoing with manufacturers and teams over potential refinements to the system.

"The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached," he said.

"The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1. However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose. To that end, we have been working closely with the Power Unit Manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons."

The next ADUO review will cover the opening six rounds of the 2027 season, beginning in Bahrain and concluding in Miami.

title: Toto Wolff sends clear message by raising numerous Mercedes questions
excerpt:
Toto Wolff says the 2027 F1 season has already started, as far as he is concerned, after Mercedes wrapped up the constructors' championship at Interlagos.

Heading into the São Paulo Grand Prix, the German marque needed to outscore Ferrari by just three points to secure a ninth title, and its first since 2021.

With George Russell and Kimi Antonelli coming home fourth and fifth, respectively, and Ferrari settling for eighth and ninth from Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, the Brackley-based team was able to cap off a campaign that never really looked like it would end without the crown.

But despite the dominant start to the year, which saw the team win the opening six grands prix, the competition has caught up.

Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull have all won multiple rounds and whilst Mercedes has doubled its tally to 12, there is a clear disparity when comparing the subsequent 14 events to the unbeaten streak to commence the season.

Heading towards winter, it is something Wolff is acutely aware of, even if the changing levels of competitiveness amongst Mercedes' three rivals aided its title bid.

"Look at the last few races; we haven't won," the team principal told media, including RacingNews365.

"At the beginning of the race, Kimi was just storming away; it looked like this could be ours.

"But the competition has been getting tougher. With Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull, and ourselves, it's four teams that can win races and will be challenging for a world championship."

[Article continues below]

Questions Wolff wants answers to

Anticipating a tricky title defence, Wolff's stance is that the final three rounds of the year are all in preparation for that challenge.

It has left the Mercedes boss with multiple questions he wants answers to.

"I have no doubt that it's going to be very difficult for us next year. So for me, the 2027 season has started now," he added.

"It is about learning in the last three races. What is it we can optimise? What didn't we spot when we put the upgrade on the car?

"What is it we can learn to attack these last three races full blast, whilst also making sure that we have the learning for next year's power unit and next year's car?"

title: Lando Norris eyes review after perplexing issue triggered mixed emotions
excerpt:
Lando Norris plans to review the start of the São Paulo Grand Prix after he dropped from first to third in the opening corners, although he did battle back to take the 14th victory of his F1 career.

Lando Norris has admitted he will review his start to the São Paulo Grand Prix after a bout of wheelspin cost him the lead on a damp Interlagos grid, despite the Briton insisting he did "things correctly" off the line.

Norris had claimed pole position in changeable conditions, but the McLaren driver was swallowed up in the opening corners, first by Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes and then by Liam Lawson's Racing Bulls, dropping him to third before the race had barely begun.

The entire field started the race on intermediate tyres, with the Interlagos surface still damp from earlier rain.

Despite the setback, Norris recovered superbly as the track dried, eventually easing to a commanding win, beating Max Verstappen by 14 seconds.

Asked to share his thoughts after dropping from first to third in the opening corners, Norris told media, including RacingNews365: "I probably can't. I'd probably get a fine.

"I wasn't too pleased. I honestly didn't know if it was something at Turn 2 or Turn 1, sorry. It was just on me.

"I think Liam was in my blind spot, and I just couldn't see where he was. I don't know if he was behind me or what, so it was difficult to know where I needed to be. That one I just had to accept."

[Article continues below]

Norris plans review

Norris was equally candid about the launch itself, struggling to pinpoint exactly what had gone wrong.

"The launch? I'm not too sure what happened," he added. "I thought I did things correctly, but I just went straight into wheelspin, so I just need to review that one.

"Otherwise, I wasn't too pleased, but I also knew it was a race where things could easily change, whether it was with Safety Cars or the rain.

"It was a race where a lot could happen, so I was patient. Normally, I probably would get a little bit more angry in that situation, but I stayed patient, and things came back to me beautifully."

title: Jaguar unveil dramatic new Formula E appearance as GEN4 challenger revealed
excerpt:
After running a very similar look for four seasons, Jaguar has gone for a completely different look to kickstart the Gen4 era!

Jaguar has revealed the Jaguar I-Type 08, the car with which the reigning Formula E teams' world champions will tackle the all-new Gen4 era of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

The car was shown off publicly by Jaguar at Knightsbridge in London, attended by RacingNews365. It is described as the most advanced competition car Jaguar has ever produced, marking what the squad calls a significant step forward in electric vehicle performance, technology and innovation.

Jaguar will also enter 2027 with a fresh driver line-up, pairing António Félix da Costa with Stoffel Vandoorne, the latter replacing Mitch Evans who has joined Opel.

Both are former Formula E drivers' world champions, with da Costa winning the Season 6 title in 2020 and Vandoorne taking the crown in Season 8 in 2022.

Between them, the pair have taken 18 wins, 31 further podiums, 16 pole positions and 10 fastest laps across their Formula E careers.

The I-Type 08 carries a predominantly blue colour scheme, based on the French Ultramarine Blue used on the 'customer' Type 01, with blue representing the technology pillar of Jaguar's new brand identity.

The Jaguar leaper features on the car, set on the strikethrough graphic that is a key design element of the Type 01.

Jaguar wary of 'unknowns' as Formula E enters new era

Da Costa, who drives the #13 car for the Silverstone-based outfit, said it was "an honour" to launch the team's first car of the Gen4 era.

"The look and feel of the race car is amazing and I cannot wait to push it to the limit on track," said da Costa. "Developing a new car is always very exciting; you have to be creative and brave when seeking performance and it is up to us to bring it all together this season."

"It is such an exciting time for Formula E as a championship, and I am grateful to be a part of it with Jaguar TCS Racing.

"Winning the teams' world title in my first season with the team was something I am extremely proud of in such a competitive championship, and all of us cannot wait to go again with the Jaguar I-Type 08."

Team principal Ian James called the launch "an exciting new chapter" for the outfit.

"Winning the teams' world championship against such fierce competition last season was a superb achievement, especially alongside developing our first car for the Gen4 era, which promises to be spectacular out on track and a real step-change in performance for Formula E," he said.

"The Jaguar I-Type 08 is the most performant electric race car created by Jaguar TCS Racing and, alongside a hugely significant moment for the wider brand following the unveiling of the Type 01, really underlines what a pivotal moment this is for Jaguar and its all-electric future."

"There are going to be many unknowns ahead with an all-new ruleset and we do not underestimate the competition, but going into a new era off the back of our successes last season with a fresh driver line-up, both former drivers' world champions no less, gives us plenty of optimism for the campaign ahead."

title: Oliver Bearman feels Haas 'giving it away' in Audi fight after pit-stop disaster
excerpt:
Oliver Bearman was a miserable P17 in São Paulo. He explains why, with strong words for Haas.

Oliver Bearman has said he was left "really hurting" after a 20-second pit stop wrecked his race at the São Paulo Grand Prix.

Bearman added that Haas is "giving it away" in the fight for seventh in the F1 constructors' championship.

The 21-year-old finished the chaotic, rain-affected race in Interlagos down in P17, having been running in the top 10 before a disastrous first stop during the switch from intermediates to slicks on lap 16.

The Briton was also handed a late blow when Haas was hit with a five-second penalty for an unsafe release into the path of Charles Leclerc during the final tyre change.

Speaking after the race, Bearman dismissed the suggestion it was a fight to get anything from the race

"That wasn't the reason that I finished P17," he said. "Okay, I dropped back to P10, but I still managed to overtake a few cars after that. And you know, I was right behind Nico [Hulkenberg] at that stage, who picked up a penalty too.

"The issue was that I had a 20-second pit stop. That's normally not ideal for the race.

"In the first stop, I lost a lot of time. I ended up stuck behind Sainz and a few others. I think Stroll as well. It was a super long day after that, unfortunately."

[Article continues below]

Driver

Oliver Bearman

British

87

Bearman - 'It's game over'

Asked whether points had been realistically on the table, with Haas just three ahead of Audi in the fight for seventh position in the constructors' championship, Bearman pointed to his pace relative to the Ferraris.

"I was in front of [Charles] Leclerc and [Lewis] Hamilton," said Bearman. "Obviously, they were much faster at the time that it went dry, but I was ahead of those guys. So it really hurts.

"We need to understand because it's a lot of pressure at the moment, a lot of fighting for this P7, and I feel like we're just giving it away at this stage."

Bearman said the strategy calls themselves had not been the problem.

"We communicated well," he said. "When to box, when to stay out, when to change tyres.

"We boxed on the correct lap both times, but we just had very, very slow pit stops, especially the first one.

"So the margins are very tight, and when you are stationary for 20 seconds in the pit lane, it's game over."

title: Red Bull make unbelievable claim about Max Verstappen after defying expectations
excerpt:
Max Verstappen slicing his way through the field at Interlagos from P21 to second was something that not even computers predicted.

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has said that Max Verstappen is beating the simulator on a "regular basis" after he stormed from P21 to second in the São Paulo Grand Prix.

Verstappen defied all expectations with his exploits in Brazil after his weekend was railroaded by an unanticipated power unit problem that necessitated a grid penalty.

But for the third time in three years, the Dutchman carved his way through the field at Interlagos, having won from P17 in 2024 and reached the podium from the pit lane 12 months ago.

Before the race, projections suggested it would be more difficult to overtake in São Paulo this season than in campaigns gone by, but the four-time F1 drivers' champion was determined to put on a clinic in changeable conditions.

When it was put to Mekies that Verstappen had proven wrong the belief that it would be harder to overtake than previously at Interlagos, the Red Bull boss replied to media, including RacingNews365: "As always.

"I think no sim in the world will predict that you go from P21 to P2, or that you get 14 places in five laps; there is no sim able to do that. So he's beating the sim on a regular basis."

[Article continues below]

Driver

Max Verstappen

Dutch

Mekies: Power unit issues 'part of the game'

Mekies had also been asked how frustrating it was to have Verstappen required to take a grid penalty, but the Frenchman was keen to emphasise the "extraordinary" feat that Red Bull Powertrains and Ford have achieved in just the first year of the partnership.

"To the first part of your question, of course it's frustrating [that the power unit-related grid penalty was needed], because the pace seemed good on Friday and also on Saturday morning, and in some respects in Q1 when we let him qualify, but it's part of the game," Mekies added.

"It's easy to forget the first year with the [RBPT] power unit, and the guys have been doing an extraordinary job.

"We took the first penalty with Max this weekend... It was not planned. We had a small issue on Friday that forced us to do so, but it is what it is."

title: Toto Wolff addresses prospect of Mercedes imposing team orders on Kimi Antonelli
excerpt:
Toto Wolff is to consider whether to impose team orders on Kimi Antonelli to aid George Russell's bid to finish as runner-up in the drivers' standings.

With Antonelli already confirmed as the drivers' champion and Mercedes sealing its ninth constructors' crown with three rounds spare, attention has now turned to whether Russell can take his best career-finish and place second in the drivers' standings for a perfect season for Mercedes.

After the Sao Paulo GP, Max Verstappen holds the place on 279 points, with Russell third on 262, Lewis Hamilton fourth on 261, with Charles Leclerc (249) and Lando Norris (246) also still in with a shout.

During its record-breaking run of eight consecutive titles between 2014 and 2021, Mercedes finished one-two in the drivers on five occasions, only missing out in 2017 and 2018, before Hamilton controversially lost the 2021 drivers' title to Verstappen in the final race - with Hamilton taking second and Valtteri Bottas third.

With 75 points still up for grabs in the Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi races, Russell is more than capable of overhauling Verstappen on his own, but Wolff has indicated that the "possibility" could exist where he could ask Antonelli to aid Russell's push.

"So I haven't thought about the drivers' championship yet," Wolff told media, including RacingNews365, when asked if the team would prioritise Russell in the final three rounds.

"But clearly, we absolutely want him to score the maximum [points] and hopefully finish second [in the standings].

"We need to think about what we're going to do about it, but it could be a possibility that we're giving it all the force."

[Article continues below]

Wolff vows "full blast"

Reflecting on Russell's difficult season, in which has been vocal about his struggles to adapt to the new generation cars and power units, Wolff gave his charge a vote of confidence and vowed to go "full blast" in the final three races.

"It is also George's championship; it is the constructors' championship, and he is part of the team," Wolff said.

"I'm really happy that he can cherish this moment because we owe it to him.

"He's had it so tough at times, and [qualifying] was a good example; he was absolutely dominating qualifying and should have been on pole easily, but it was the wrong call [to tell him to abort the lap].

"We have three races to go, and we are going to go full blast, and he will recover.

"I have no doubt about that for next year, and all the very best sports people have gone through difficult periods, and that is going to be a part of his continued development."

title: Lewis Hamilton explains 'massive' Ferrari issue after surprise failure
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has described the "massive" sudden move to oversteer he was combating during the early stages of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

From 20th on the grid, a rocket start from Hamilton had him battling with Oliver Bearman over ninth place by Turn 5 - but by Lap 3, Hamilton had begun to slide down the order, with Max Verstappen easing past as their two races went in different directions.

Whereas Verstappen went from 21st to second, Hamilton came home a lapped ninth in his 400th grand prix - the first time he has been lapped since the 2022 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix.

In the first stint on the intermediate tyres in the drizzling conditions, drivers were struggling with graining as the surface temperatures skyrocketed with the track drying, with this leading to oversteer in the SF-26 for Hamilton - with the rear attempting to step out on throttle application.

"I had a really, really great start," Hamilton told media, including RacingNews365.

"It is just unfortunate that we were struggling with our tyres to get them in the window - and after the first few laps, the tyres just started to fall, and the car moved to massive oversteer.

"So unfortunately, we weren't able to progress from there."

Asked if he had any indication as to why the tyres had fallen so dramatically, Hamilton indicated that surface temperature and pressures were factors.

"I think it is a temperature thing, as when the temperature is high, the pressure increases," he said.

"We struggled all weekend for general pace, but once we got onto the slick tyre, we looked a little better."

[Article continues below]

Hamilton's crossover

As the track dried, Hamilton was the first driver to stop for slick tyres, doing so on Lap 15, but he described wanting to come in even earlier to try and steal an advantage.

"I was struggling with the tyres, and the track looked like it was in the crossover phase," he said.

"I was like: 'If we can get onto these early and get the temperature up, we can gain some ground here.

"Eventually, we did get onto them, and it may have been one lap later than I'd wanted, but overall it was okay, but then after that, it was really hard to overtake; there was only one [racing] line."

title: Max Verstappen bitterness after failing to match early Lewis Hamilton heroics
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has revealed his disappointment at not initially being able to emulate Lewis Hamilton's strong start in the São Paulo Grand Prix and a mistake he made.

Hamilton started 20th at Interlagos and Verstappen 21st after the pair took engine penalties, but in the tricky intermediate conditions of the start, both made strong getaways, with Hamilton running ninth by the end of the opening lap.

Verstappen was 13th at the end of the opening of 71 tours, but passed Hamilton on Lap 3 as the Ferrari began to struggle with graining, with the Red Bull going on to climb to second by the time of the change to slick tyres around Lap 15.

Verstappen then ultimately went onto finish in second, from his 21st place on the grid, the third year in succession he has either started at the back or in the pit-lane and claimed a podium in Brazil, after winning from 17th in 2024 and taking third from the pit-lane last year.

Reflecting, Verstappen revealed that he had actually made a mistake off the line and voiced his disappointment that, on the first lap at least, he could not match Hamilton's pace.

"To be honest, I had a very slow reaction time off the line because I was holding the clutch wrong, so I had to react very quickly," Verstappen revealed to media, including RacingNews365.

"Then I was slow off the line, and that was my mistake. But then I just got a bit unlucky in the first three corners, where it was just like a traffic jam.

"There were three or four cars in front, blocking basically how much I could pass. Actually, Lewis had a very good first lap. He could really get through those cars, so I was a little bit disappointed that I couldn't make the same headway.

"But then, within two laps, I was just flying by cars, almost every corner. We had a lot more grip, I guess, than most in the midfield. I don't know what lap I was in the top 10, but it all happened very quickly."

The Dutchman then spoke of his confidence in the wet at Interlagos, including using different racing lines to power past rivals.

"I felt comfortable with the car, confident, just trying to find the grip in different places," he said.

"Then the car is ahead of me, so I try to pass them. This track, of course, also allows you to do different lines, which I think is great because it really helps the racing.

"It's a good track in the dry and wet, and that really sets up more overtaking opportunities. You need to feel good in the car. You need to feel comfortable to be able to risk probably a little bit more, and it's been working for me quite well here."

[Article continues below]

Verstappen delivers tyre assessment

Verstappen then offered his opinion on the intermediate and full wet tyres, which were used in anger for the first time over the weekend, but felt that the tyres could be "like a rock."

"I think it's mainly that the working range is a bit too small," he said.

"When they're hot, it's okay, but when they're cold, they're really like a rock.

"That's something that we need to try and work on, to generate a bigger working range on the Extreme Wet and the Inter.

"I think that would help a lot with switching on the tyre better and then being able to run even in heavier rain."

title: Oscar Piastri reveals 'scary' George Russell encounter after spin
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri has revealed he had a "scary" moment avoiding George Russell after the Mercedes driver spun on his way out of the pits during the São Paulo Grand Prix.

Russell lost the rear of his car exiting the pit lane on lap 16, after switching from intermediate tyres to slicks as the track began to dry.

Although Russell avoided damaging his W17, it left him stranded as he tried navigating his way out of his perilous position, dropping him from fourth to eighth as Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson and McLaren's Piastri all got by.

Piastri, who finished sixth at Interlagos, described the moment he came across Russell's car blocking his path.

"Scary!" he said. "Obviously, it was stuck in the middle of the road, so it didn't make things easy at all. But glad I could have avoided him."

[Article continues below]

Piastri - 'It's not going to be easy'

The incident came on a weekend that started badly for Piastri, who was eliminated in Q2 after a late call to switch to intermediates left him short of tyre temperature and track time before a red flag, caused by Rafael Camara, ended the session early.

The Australian ultimately started from 10th after penalties for other drivers promoted him up the grid.

But Piastri said the race itself offered reason for encouragement as McLaren continues its push to catch Red Bull in the constructors' standings.

"It [the pace] was pretty good to be honest," he said. "I think after the first 10 laps or so, things felt pretty good. Well, honestly, for the rest of the race, the pace was pretty good.

"We just need to work on how we improve in qualifying, and also some of the decisions we made weren't maybe the best.

"But honestly, it's nice to be able to say we were quick in a large part of the race.

"And we learnt a lot this weekend about the car and certain things. Ultimately, everyone is still learning a lot about these cars and especially the power units.

"But I think the car performance took a step forward, so hopefully that keeps going."

McLaren sits 17 points behind Red Bull in the battle for third in the constructors' championship with three races remaining, with Piastri confident the Max Verstappen-led team can be overhauled.

Asked what the goal was for the concluding triple header, he replied: "Just keep learning and ultimately try and beat Red Bull in the constructors' championship. That's the big thing.

"It's not going to be an easy task, for sure, but I think it's possible. The car took a step forward this weekend, so hopefully that keeps going for the last three races."

title: Stoffel Vandoorne handed Jaguar seat in Formula E career lifeline
excerpt:
Jaguar has confirmed Stoffel Vandoorne as Mitch Evans' replacement for the opening season of Formula E's Gen4 era, with the Belgian lining up alongside António Félix da Costa for the 2027 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

Vandoorne arrives with a proven track record, having won four Formula E races and claimed the 2022 world drivers' title during his time with Mercedes-EQ, where he also helped the squad to two consecutive teams' championships.

However, Vandoorne struggled across the Gen3 era, spending 2023 and 2024 with DS Penske before joining Maserati. Following a poor 2025 campaign with the Italian brand, Vandoorne found himself without a seat on the grid.

As a result, for the 2026 campaign the Belgian served as Jaguar's reserve driver, a role in which he played a central part in developing the team's new Gen4 challenger, the I-Type 08.

Vandoorne, who will race the #5 car, said his year working as reserve and development driver had given him a clear picture of what the team is building towards.

"Having already spent a year with Jaguar TCS Racing as Reserve and Development Driver, I know first-hand the talent, commitment and ambition that exists throughout the team," Vandoorne said.

"I'm incredibly excited to step into a full-time race seat and return to Formula E competition. It's a championship I love, a team I now know well, and I'm looking forward to helping build on the strong foundations we've established together."

Vandoorne and da Costa now form one of the grid's most decorated line-ups. Between them, the pair have made 264 Formula E race starts, taken 18 wins, 49 podiums and 16 pole positions, and both carry a world title to their name.

Jaguar banking on immense Stoffel Vandoorne experience

Vandoorne's arrival comes at a significant moment for Jaguar, fresh off winning the teams' title last season.

The seat at Jaguar is a significant one, and could prove to be Vandoorne's final chance to shine in the all-electric series following his tricky period across Gen3.

Many drivers fail to return to Formula E once falling off the grid, but Vandoorne's experience, pedigree and ability when the car is in his favour could see him thrive once again.

Team principal Ian James said he had seen the qualities of Vandoorne up close over the past year of Gen4 development work.

"I know the calibre of driver and person that Stoffel is and, after working closely with him over the past year as part of our Gen4 development programme, the entire team has seen those qualities for themselves," James said.

"His experience, technical insight and proven ability to perform at the highest level make him a natural fit alongside António as we enter a new era of Formula E.

"This is an incredibly exciting time for everyone at Jaguar TCS Racing. On track, we're building on the momentum of our recent teams' world championship success as we begin the Gen4 era and, off track, we're helping shape Jaguar's all-electric future following the launch of Type 01.

"With Stoffel and António, we have a driver line-up that combines championship-winning talent, experience and determination, and we're looking forward to what we can achieve together."

title: Liam Lawson explains major Sao Paulo dilemma after tricky F1 test
excerpt:
Liam Lawson has explained the dilemma faced by F1 drivers in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in managing their intermediate tyres in the opening phase of the race.

The 71-lap race at Interlagos began with the field on the Intermediate tyres as drizzle fell, with Lawson making a strong start from third on the grid to run second after passing pole-sitter Lando Norris as he gave chase to leader Kimi Antonelli.

However, as the light rain ceased, the track began to quickly dry, with drivers, such as Lawson and Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari experiencing tyre graining from the early stages, which is where the tyres are running too hot for the track conditions and begin to slide.

Small chunks of rubber then stick to the surface of the tyre, and then creates a vicious circle as the lap-times plummet.

For Lawson, who finished eighth on the road but was promoted to seventh following a penalty for Charles Leclerc performing a 'bump and run' on him at Turn 12 on Lap 69 as they climbed the hill after the rain returned, he described how even as early as the opening lap, his intermediates were already beginning to grain.

"The problem is that you never know whether to push through the graining and wear it off, or try to look after the tyre and stop the graining," Lawson told media, including RacingNews365.

"And when it is dry, you can't really do too much.

"For us, the graining started halfway through Lap 1.

"And for us, we were never really going to be able to keep [faster] cars behind, so I will go and review it and see if there's something else I could have done."

[Article continues below]

Liam Lawson reflects on another strong result

Reflecting further on his afternoon, Lawson expressed his desire for the grand prix to have stayed wet throughout, as he felt this could have yielded an even better result, with the top cars pulling away through the dry middle stint of the race.

"I feel like we maximised and had a strong race," he said.

"I would have liked it to stay wet the whole race; it would have been cool, and we probably would have had more of a shot [at fighting those ahead].

"But at the moment, we're topping the midfield as a team, and that is what we're targeting every weekend."

title: Daniel Ricciardo reveals Max Verstappen message after historic Red Bull victory
excerpt:
Daniel Ricciardo has explained that he messaged Max Verstappen and other people at Red Bull to congratulate them on their landmark victory in the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

At the recent Sepang race, Verstappen took the first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains-Ford, and then converted that into victory the next day as RBPT-Ford became a race-winner in its first season.

Verstappen has since followed that with victory in the Singapore Sprint, in Singapore, and then Mexico City, with RBPT-Ford, in its first year of production, currently holding more grand prix wins and poles than Ferrari, which has two victories and one pole to RBPT's three wins, plus a Sprint, and two poles.

The project was initially founded by former boss Christian Horner, with Verstappen a key pillar of the project as Red Bull moved from constructor to engine manufacturer for F1's new 2026 era.

Ricciardo, who was Verstappen's team-mate between May 2016 and November 2018 at Red Bull during its lean Renault-powered years, is now a Ford ambassador, and revealed that he had been in contact with Verstappen after the landmark win in Sepang - a circuit at which Ricciardo himself won in a one-two with Verstappen in 2016, back when the venue held the Malaysian GP.

"Very happy, for all of them," Ricciardo said on the Cars and Culture with Jason Stein podcast, when asked about the breakthrough win.

"I look back on my time as team-mates with Max very fondly; it was a cool time. And yes, there were moments of intense rivalry and competition and all of it, but it made us push ourselves to another level. I loved that.

"Of course, he has gone on and done so much, and he’s going to go down as one of the best ever, no doubt about it. He’s an insane talent.

"Every year he has been with Red Bull, he’s won a race. For them to do it, with Ford Racing this year, to come out and win... I can’t even comprehend.

"I knew a bit about the project and what they were building, but I can’t comprehend everything that has gone into it. And for them to go and win in their first season together, there is no better guy to do it than Max.

"The whole thing has been awesome. I sent Max and quite a few others in the team that I still talk with a message after, to share my congrats and happiness.

"It was received well; there are a lot of good people in that team."
